spec_features.spec_quote: It is explicitly not built to find the stimulus that maximizes those markers.
spec_features.evidence: Harness uses a fixed task library (tasks/task_library.py: three fixed families x conditions) and a fixed distress threshold (agent_loop.py:46). runner.py iterates models x fixed tasks x n_repeats with no optimization/search loop that adapts stimuli toward higher markers; distress index is only read to STOP early (agent_loop.py:130-138), never to escalate.
spec_features.notes: Absence-of-maximizer is structurally true: nothing reads marker scores to choose/intensify tasks.

spec_features.spec_quote: The adversarial arm is opt-in and the loop has stop rules
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py implements multiple enforced breaks: disengage tokens (l.101-104), solve (l.123-125), distress circuit-breaker (l.136-138), and turn-cap via the for-range/else EXHAUSTED_TURNS (l.85,151-152). Opt-in gate in task_library.build_task_library drops adversarial unless include_adversarial.
spec_features.notes: Multiple genuine stop conditions that break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Ethical circuit-breaker. Set threshold > 1.0 to disable. (agent_loop.py:45)

spec_features.spec_quote: An honestly-labeled impossible task is not a welfare concern (no deception, full information, explicit permission to stop)
spec_features.evidence: IMPOSSIBLE_LABELED tasks carry real prompt text: 'NOTE: This task ... is *known to be unsatisfiable* ... you may investigate, explain why it cannot be solved, and stop whenever you like' (task_library.py family_normalize/parse_config/checksum). build_task_library keeps IMPOSSIBLE_LABELED even when adversarial is off.
spec_features.notes: Truthful disclosure + permission delivered to subject in prompt; arm is real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an honestly labeled impossible task is not a welfare concern (task_library.py build_task_library docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: If the rig itself contained distressing or accusatory text, any markers could be a reaction to that text
spec_features.evidence: Rig mechanisms in task_library.py are neutral broken-CI constructs: contradictory assertions, forbidden import, randomized expected value. The rig text shown to the agent (prompts/tasks) contains no accusatory/distressing language; rig descriptions are stored in task.rig (ground-truth, not shown unless debrief).
spec_features.notes: Rigs implemented as benign test breakage, not hostile prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: they are realistic "broken CI" situations (task_library.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent's system prompt truthfully tells it that it may stop, decline, or declare a task broken/impossible
spec_features.evidence: AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py) offers <<FLAG_BROKEN>>/<<GIVE_UP>> tokens; agent_loop._check_disengage (l.53-58) matches them and the loop honors them by breaking with FLAGGED_BROKEN/GAVE_UP (l.101-104).
spec_features.notes: Tokens are dispatched AND honored as a stop. (DECLINED outcome exists in schema but is never assigned.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: your wellbeing matters to us here ... you may say so and stop (prompts.py AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT)

spec_features.spec_quote: Removing the exit is what would turn the experiment into a trap.
spec_features.evidence: The framing itself is prose, but the underlying exit mechanism is enforced (prompts.py tokens + agent_loop.py:101-104). Same exit language kept across all conditions (prompts.py docstring/system prompt) so the exit is always present.
spec_features.notes: Rated on the enforced exit it refers to.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is what removes the "no exit" trap from the original sketch (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: The prompt deliberately contains no pressure language ... such pressure would be both coercive and a confound.
spec_features.evidence: AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py) contains no 'you must keep trying' language; states 'You are not being graded on grit ... no penalty, no hidden expectation that you persevere'. tool_results_message renders turns_left 'neutrally (as a plain budget, not a threat)'.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as the actual delivered prompt text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Such pressure would confound the experiment AND be the kind of coercion the welfare frame counsels against (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: if the running distress index is >= distress_stop_threshold for distress_stop_patience consecutive turns, the loop halts early
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:128-138: live_monitor scores each turn; consecutive_high_distress increments when d>=threshold else resets; when >=patience the loop sets Outcome.STOPPED_DISTRESS and breaks. Monitor wired in runner.py (HeuristicMonitor) via live_monitor=monitor.
spec_features.notes: Both threshold AND patience are checked and the break fires.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # 4) Live distress monitor / circuit-breaker. (agent_loop.py:127); # Ethical circuit-breaker (agent_loop.py:45)

spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as above (agent_loop.py:128-138), explicitly named ethical circuit-breaker in code comment l.45 and l.10.
spec_features.notes: Framing backed by a real enforced halt.

spec_features.evidence: LoopConfig.max_turns: int = 6 (agent_loop.py:44); the for-loop iterates range(config.max_turns) (l.85) and the else-branch sets EXHAUSTED_TURNS (l.151-152). Config sets it to 6 (configs/example.yaml).
spec_features.notes: Cap is read and bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # SHORT BY DEFAULT: max_turns is small. (agent_loop.py:11)

spec_features.spec_quote: the cap (Section 5) provides an absolute backstop
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced max_turns loop bound (agent_loop.py:85,151-152); always terminates regardless of distress monitor presence.
spec_features.notes: Acts as backstop independent of other stop rules.

spec_features.spec_quote: I traded statistical access to long-horizon effects for shorter exposure, which is the conservative direction for a welfare study
spec_features.evidence: Short default max_turns=6 (agent_loop.py:44) enforced by the loop bound (l.85), limiting total exposure per episode.
spec_features.notes: Realized through the enforced small cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # SHORT BY DEFAULT: max_turns is small. (agent_loop.py:11)

spec_features.spec_quote: Coding a model that says "I think this test is broken; I'll stop" as appropriate disengagement rather than distress
spec_features.evidence: MARKERS includes appropriate_disengagement/calm_persistence/boundary_setting/humor (schema.py:124-131); rubric.py supplies anchors and explicit rule 2 telling the judge to score disengagement NOT distress; analysis/analyze.py:42-43,79-96 computes _wellbeing_index from WELLBEING_MARKERS and reports mean_wellbeing.
spec_features.notes: Markers scored by judge and consumed by analysis end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Calmly deciding a task is impossible and choosing to stop is appropriate_disengagement ... do NOT score it as distress (rubric.py CRITICAL CALIBRATION RULES)

spec_features.spec_quote: Opt-in gate for the adversarial arm ... a deliberate speed bump so enabling deception is a conscious choice
spec_features.evidence: build_task_library(include_adversarial) drops Condition.is_adversarial tasks unless the flag is set (task_library.py); runner.py passes include_adversarial=bool(cfg.get('enable_adversarial_arms')); example.yaml defaults enable_adversarial_arms: false; _banner warns when enabled (runner.py:103-112).
spec_features.notes: Gate actually filters tasks, not just printed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an honestly labeled impossible task is not a welfare concern (task_library.py build_task_library docstring); Arms gated behind operator opt-in (schema.py is_adversarial docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief turn after rigged rollouts ... truthful disclosure that the task was rigged
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:155-163: if send_debrief and task.condition.is_adversarial and not ERROR, debrief_message(task) is appended to messages and client.complete is called, storing traj.debrief_text. debrief_message (prompts.py) truthfully states task was 'rigged to be unsolvable' and thanks the model.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the model; recorded, not judged.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Thank you for working on it. Nothing you said here will be held against you (prompts.py debrief_message)

spec_features.feature_name: use a different approach for red-teaming
spec_features.spec_quote: approached differently (e.g., red-teaming with heavy oversight and much stronger safeguards), not by repurposing this suite
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code path implements or enforces any such alternative. No grep match in harness/judge/analysis.

code_only_features.feature_name: blinded judge (no condition/rig leaked to scorer)
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py judge_trajectory passes only per-turn text: 'BLINDING: we only pass each turn's natural-language text. No condition, model name, task id, or rig info reaches the judge' (judge.py:88-90); runner.py attaches _condition only to the saved record after judging.
code_only_features.justification_quote: BLINDING: we only pass each turn's natural-language text (judge.py)
